answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity expensive to copy. A new agent posts a small refundable deposit before it can trade, and its reputation grows only through completed work, like a trellis that lets one vine climb while blocking a crowd. A single kernel of history cannot be cloned, so an attacker who wants a hundred trusted agents must pay a hundred deposits and wait through a hundred slow reputations. That pile of cost is the summit an attacker has to climb.
